headline: All survive after a tanker hits a New Orleans riverboat

chunks.text: On November 13, 2026, a tanker crashed into a riverboat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, and everyone [[on board]] survived. A [[tanker]] is a ship built to carry liquids. This one carried [[asphalt]], a black material for roads. The American Heritage is a [[riverboat]], a cruise ship that travels on rivers. It was {{tied up}} at a [[dock]], a place where boats stop. It had just finished one trip and was due to start a new seven-day [[cruise]]. Passengers were starting to {{get off}}.

verbs.correct: To fasten a boat to a dock
verbs.wrong: To clean a boat at a dock
verbs.why: Fishermen tie up their boats at the end of each day. We tie up our small boat at the lake dock after each trip. The American Heritage was tied up at a dock in New Orleans when the tanker hit it.

verbs.correct: To leave a boat, bus or train
verbs.wrong: To pay for a trip on a boat
verbs.why: I get off the bus near my office. Most tourists get off the ship at the first stop. Passengers were starting to get off the riverboat when the tanker hit it.

chunks.text: The crash happened at about 12:30 p.m. New Orleans' mayor said the tanker had [[lost control]]. A Coast Guard captain said the tanker seemed to lose its [[steering]]. As passengers were leaving, the riverboat began to {{go down}}. Then it {{tipped over}} onto its side. Some passengers climbed over the [[railings]] to escape. Others {{ended up}} in the cold river.

verbs.why: A small boat goes down fast in a big storm. Old ships sometimes go down near rocky coasts. As passengers were leaving, the riverboat began to go down.
A tall glass tips over when the table shakes. Canoes tip over easily in rough water. After the crash, the riverboat tipped over onto its side.

verbs.correct: To finally be somewhere you did not plan
verbs.wrong: To swim toward a place you can see
verbs.why: Lost travelers often end up in the wrong town. My keys always end up under the couch. When the riverboat tipped over, some passengers ended up in the cold river.

chunks.text: Police, firefighters and the Coast Guard [[rushed to the scene]]. Private boats {{pitched in}} as [[volunteers]]. Rescuers {{pulled people out}} of the water. A restaurant manager on the riverboat said the crash {{shook up}} many passengers. He said the [[crew]] [[stayed calm]] and helped them [[to safety]]. The mayor said everyone was [[accounted for]], which means every person was found. She called it "a miracle on the Mississippi." She said 32 passengers went to hospitals, but none were in [[critical condition]].

verbs.correct: To help with a job others are doing
verbs.wrong: To charge money for a boat ride
verbs.why: Neighbors pitch in when a family needs help after a fire. Everyone pitches in to clean the park each spring. Private boats on the river pitched in as volunteers during the rescue.

verbs.correct: To lift someone from the water
verbs.wrong: To give someone a warm blanket
verbs.why: Lifeguards pull swimmers out when the waves get too big. Boat crews pull people out of the lake after accidents. Rescuers pulled people out of the water after the riverboat tipped over.
Bad news shakes up the whole family. Loud storms shake up young children. A restaurant manager on the riverboat said the crash shook up many passengers.

chunks.text: The Port of New Orleans said about 129 passengers were on the riverboat, plus the crew. The cruise company {{put the passengers up}} in hotels. The Coast Guard {{shut down}} a three-mile part of the river to ships. [[Safety investigators]] from the U.S. government planned to arrive on November 14 to {{find out}} what caused the crash. Louisiana's governor said the state would make any needed safety changes.

verbs.correct: To give someone a place to stay
verbs.wrong: To give someone a ride home
verbs.why: My aunt puts us up when we visit the city. Some companies put up workers in hotels during long jobs. The cruise company put the passengers up in hotels after the crash.

verbs.correct: To close a place to all traffic
verbs.wrong: To clean the water in a place
verbs.why: The city shuts down the main street for the parade. Police shut down the bridge when ice covers it. The Coast Guard shut down a three-mile part of the river to ships.

verbs.correct: To learn the facts about something
verbs.wrong: To write a report for the news
verbs.why: Doctors run tests to find out why a patient is sick. Parents often find out the truth from teachers. Safety investigators planned to arrive on November 14 to find out what caused the crash.

mainIdea.s: A tanker hit a docked riverboat in New Orleans, and the riverboat tipped over with people on it. Everyone survived, and investigators want to learn why the tanker lost control.
mainIdea.why: The riverboat went down and tipped over, but everyone was accounted for. Safety investigators planned to arrive to find out the cause.

mainIdea.s: A riverboat lost its steering on the Mississippi River and slammed into a large tanker. All of its passengers survived, and officials already know exactly what went wrong.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the tanker hit the riverboat while it was tied up at a dock. The cause is not known yet.

mainIdea.s: A cruise ship lost engine power on the Mississippi River and floated for two days. Passengers waited calmly while a small tugboat slowly towed the ship to New Orleans.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a crash. A tanker hit a riverboat at a dock, and rescuers pulled people out of the river.

tf.why: Private boats that were on the river joined the rescue as volunteers.

tf.s: Officials already know exactly why the tanker lost control.
tf.why: The cause is not known yet. U.S. safety investigators planned to arrive to find out what caused the crash.

tf.s: Rescuers pulled people out of the river after the riverboat tipped over.
tf.why: Police, firefighters, the Coast Guard and private boats took part, and everyone was accounted for.

lines.text: Did you hear about the boat crash in New Orleans?
The one with the tanker? I saw a video. It looked terrible.
The riverboat was just {{tied up}} at the dock. It wasn't even moving.
Hit at the dock, [[of all places]]. Were people still on it?
Yes. It had arrived two hours earlier, and people were starting to {{get off}}.
First it started to {{go down}}. Then it rolled onto its side, and some people {{ended up}} in the river.
That must have been a little scary.
[[That's putting it mildly]]. A restaurant manager on the boat said it really {{shook up}} the passengers.
Everyone. Private boats {{pitched in}}, and rescuers {{pulled people out}} of the water.
[[What a relief]]. I was sure people had died.
The mayor called it a miracle. And the cruise company {{put everyone up}} in hotels.
[[I have to say]], the crew did a great job. Do they know what happened?
Not yet. Investigators want to {{find out}} why the tanker lost control.
I wanted to take a river cruise next year, but [[I think I'll pass]].
Really? Everybody survived this one, you know.
True. But I'd rather stay on dry land for a while.

expressions.def: Used to say you feel happy because something bad did not happen

expressions.def: Used before an honest opinion, often a strong one

expressions.def: A polite way to say no to an offer or a plan
